SIRS epidemic and dynamic force-directed layout animations

animate_sirs.Rd

R-native equivalents of graph-tool's SIRS epidemic animation (animation_sirs.py, animation_zombies.py) and dynamic force-directed spatial-segregation animation (animation_dancing.py). Simulation loops execute natively in C++ and respect set.seed.

Usage

animate_sirs(graph, pos = NULL, n_steps = 120L, x = 0.001, r = 0.1, s = 0.01,
  init_state = NULL, directed = FALSE, hide_recovered = TRUE,
  fear_state = FALSE, mode = c("html", "frames", "device", "none"),
  output = NULL, width = 760L, height = 560L, fps = 12, delay = 0.05,
  open = FALSE, main = "SIRS Epidemic Animation")

animate_dynamic_layout(graph, pos = NULL, n_steps = 80L, K = 0.5, C = 0.2,
  p = 2.0, step = 0.005, n_rewire = 10L,
  mode = c("html", "frames", "device", "none"), output = NULL, width = 760L,
  height = 560L, fps = 15, delay = 0.05, open = FALSE,
  main = "Dynamic Layout & Spatial Segregation")

Arguments

graph

A graph created by graph_create.

pos

Optional \(N \times 2\) initial vertex layout matrix. Computed with sfdp_layout if NULL.

n_steps

Number of simulation steps to run (produces n_steps + 1 frames including step 0).

x

Spontaneous infection probability (S -> I) per vertex per step.

r

Recovery probability (I -> R) per vertex per step.

s

Resusceptibility probability (R -> S) per vertex per step.

init_state

Optional integer vector of length \(N\) with values in {0, 1, 2} (0 = S, 1 = I, 2 = R). Defaults to all susceptible.

directed

Logical; if TRUE and graph$directed is TRUE, infection spreads along directed edges u -> v; otherwise undirected neighbors are used.

hide_recovered

Logical; if TRUE, recovered vertices and their incident edges are hidden from the animation (matching graph-tool's animation_sirs.py).

fear_state

Logical; if TRUE, susceptible vertices adjacent to at least one infected neighbor are highlighted in amber (matching graph-tool's animation_zombies.py).

K, C, p

SFDP spring-electrical layout parameters for animate_dynamic_layout().

step

Per-frame incremental SFDP displacement step size.

n_rewire

Number of distance-shortening edge rewiring attempts per frame (preserving edge count and avoiding isolated vertices, self-loops, and parallel edges).

mode

Output mode: "html" writes a self-contained zero-dependency interactive HTML5 Canvas viewer; "frames" writes numbered PNG files to a directory; "device" animates on the active R graphics device; "none" returns the trajectory without rendering.

output

Optional destination HTML file path (mode = "html") or directory path (mode = "frames"). Defaults to a temporary path.

width, height

Canvas or PNG frame dimensions in pixels.

fps

Initial playback rate (frames per second) for mode = "html".

delay

Pause in seconds between frames when mode = "device".

open

Logical; if TRUE in an interactive R session with mode = "html", opens the generated HTML file via browseURL.

main

Animation title.

Details

Platform and display requirements:

  • mode = "html" requires no display server, GTK+, Cairo, or external R packages; the generated standalone HTML5 file runs offline in any modern web browser or RStudio Viewer with interactive play/pause, frame scrubbing, speed control, and live summary charts.

  • mode = "frames" requires R's built-in png device (available on standard macOS, Windows, and Cairo/X11-enabled Linux builds) and produces numbered PNG frames suitable for external encoders such as ffmpeg.

  • mode = "device" renders directly to the active interactive R graphics device (Quartz, X11, Windows, or RStudioGD).

Value

animate_sirs() returns an object of class "rgraphtool_sirs_animation" containing pos, states, newly_infected, fear, counts, params, mode, output, and files.

animate_dynamic_layout() returns an object of class "rgraphtool_dynamic_layout" containing positions, edges, mean_edge_length, rewired, params, mode, output, and files.

Examples

g <- graph_create(20L, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, cbind(1:20, c(2:20, 1L)))
set.seed(1)
init <- integer(20L); init[1L] <- 1L
sirs <- animate_sirs(g, n_steps = 10L, init_state = init, mode = "none")
print(sirs)
#> rgraphtool SIRS epidemic animation
#>   vertices: 20 | frames: 11 (steps = 10)
#>   rates: x = 0.001, r = 0.1, s = 0.01 | hide_recovered = TRUE | fear_state = FALSE
#>   peak infected: 8 | total new infections: 10
#>   mode: none
dyn <- animate_dynamic_layout(g, n_steps = 10L, n_rewire = 5L, mode = "none")
print(dyn)
#> rgraphtool dynamic layout animation
#>   vertices: 20 | edges: 20 | frames: 11
#>   mean edge length: 0.4603 -> 0.4532 | total rewirings: 1
#>   mode: none
